narrative:
Lending NII of about PLN 1.69B is exposed as variable-rate assets reprice with WIBOR. Mortgages (PLN 24B) are the largest book but carry the thinnest spread (2.15%). Consumer loans & cards earn 6.8% but face the statutory anti-usury APR cap.

The best risk-adjusted headroom is in SME working capital and VeloLeasing. SME credit demand is rising, VeloBank's spread sits about 35bp below the peer median for comparable risk, and nearshoring-driven equipment demand supports leasing volumes in the West.

The WIBOR-to-WIRON transition changes repricing mechanics for new mortgage contracts and has to be reflected in the margin model before FY2027 origination.

signals.title: SME Credit Demand Survey
signals.excerpt: Banks report rising SME demand for working-capital and investment loans, with credit standards broadly unchanged and spreads stable.

signals.title: WIBOR to WIRON Transition Roadmap
signals.excerpt: The National Working Group confirmed the timetable for replacing WIBOR with WIRON in new loan contracts, affecting the repricing profile of variable-rate mortgages.

signals.title: Citi Handlowy Retail Integration Completed
signals.excerpt: Migration of the Citi Handlowy retail business completed on 15 June 2026: PLN 22.1B of deposits, PLN 6B of loans, PLN 8.9B AuM and ~1,600 employees now on VeloBank systems.
